Hi IT team,

I really need help because I've made a mess of things and honestly don't know what state my setup is in anymore. I use my Wacom pen display (the 16" Cintiq on the dock) to review candidate design exercises in the ATS — I open the portfolio PDFs in the review panel and annotate/score them with the pen. All of this worked fine earlier this week.

Yesterday during a review session the pen clicks suddenly stopped landing on the scorecard — the cursor moved fine, but clicks were hitting my laptop screen instead of the pen display, so I kept annotating the wrong window. I figured it was something small and didn't want to bother you, so I tried to fix it myself. That was probably a mistake.

Things I tried, in order:
1. Restarted, replugged the USB-C cable — nothing.
2. Updated the Wacom driver to the newest version from their site.
3. That didn't help, so I rolled it back in Device Manager, then uninstalled it completely with "delete the driver software" checked (I read that on a forum, maybe that was the bad move).
4. Turned off USB power saving and toggled the "Use Windows Ink" checkbox a bunch of times.
5. Changed some registry key a YouTube video recommended (something like TabletMode or Pen... I honestly don't remember which one, and I may have changed two).
6. Made the Cintiq my main display and back again, and dropped scaling from 125% to 100% because the ATS buttons were overlapping.

Now it's much worse. Windows doesn't detect the tablet at all — there's a yellow warning triangle in Device Manager, code 28 or 43, can't tell. And the ATS review screen itself now renders broken on my laptop: the scorecard fields are huge and overlapping, and when I click to open a candidate portfolio the preview panel is just blank white. A candidate I already scored on Friday shows as "not started" in my queue now?? Maybe caching, I don't know.

This is terrible timing — I have three portfolio review sessions with the hiring panel for the Senior Product Designer role tomorrow morning (9:00 and 10:30, plus 1pm with the candidate herself to walk through her design test), and I can't score anything without the pen. The offer deadline for this candidate is Friday, so if my scorecards don't get done the whole hiring loop slips. I also can't see the results from the two sessions I already ran yesterday.

I know I shouldn't have gone into the registry, sorry about that. Can someone remote in and see what everything is set to? I didn't write down the original settings. I'm on my ThinkPad laptop with the Cintiq on the dock, and I'm at my desk all day.

Please treat this as urgent — and sorry if this is partly my fault.

Marcia
